critic.fix_suggestion: Align the wing root geometry to the fuselage by applying a translation and rotation transform at the wing's origin point. Move the wing along its local X-axis until it intersects with the fuselage side panel, and rotate it around the Y-axis to match the 15-degree sweep angle of the main body. Ensure the wing's root thickness matches the fuselage's curvature radius to eliminate the floating gap.

discrepancies.observed: The wing appears to be floating or disconnected from the fuselage at the root.
discrepancies.reference: The wing is seamlessly integrated into the main body of the aircraft.

discrepancies.observed: Engines are positioned far forward and appear detached from the wing structure.
discrepancies.reference: Engines are mounted directly onto pylons attached to the underside of the wings.

discrepancies.observed: The vertical stabilizer is disconnected from the rear fuselage.
discrepancies.reference: The tail is structurally joined to the aft section of the fuselage.

discrepancies.observed: The landing gear struts are floating beneath the fuselage and wings without clear pivot points.
discrepancies.reference: Struts are connected to specific structural hardpoints on the body and wing roots.
